title: Build the tile cache writer
type: build
status: open
assignee: lead
blocked_by: [03]
---
## Question

Turn the ticket 03 prototype into a writer that fills one MBTiles file per zoom band from the sync query, resumable after a crash.

## Plan

1. Stream tiles from `tilesource.tiles_for_batch()` instead of loading the batch.
2. Write with `INSERT OR REPLACE` inside a transaction per flush.
3. Record the last flushed tile in `cache_progress` so a rerun resumes.

## Notes

- The prototype held the whole district in memory: 1.8 GB peak for the largest district.
- Asked **q11** about the flush interval; working with the default (every 500 tiles) meanwhile.

```sh
python3 -m tilecache.write --batch tiles_shared --zoom 12-16
```

| zoom | tiles | prototype time |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | 3,904 | 4 s |
| 14 | 61,220 | 52 s |
| 16 | 978,113 | 14 min |

box-1/tile-cache/work/adr/0001-mbtiles-p:
# Store tiles in MBTiles, one file per zoom band

## Context

A directory tree for zoom 12 to 16 holds about 2 million files. Copying it to a new node took 41 minutes in the ticket 03 prototype.

## Decision

One MBTiles (SQLite) file per zoom band.

## Consequences

- A copy is 5 files; it took 3 minutes.
- Concurrent writers to one band must serialize; the writer is single-process anyway.
